title: Memory
description: Facts your agents carry into every future session. Global memories apply everywhere; project memories are only ever shown inside their own project.

write.label: Agents can write memories
write.description: While this is off, nothing agents ask to remember is kept. Their requests stay in the chats they were written in, and switching this back on applies them — a pause delays memory, it does not lose it.

read.label: Mix memory into prompts
read.description: While this is off, no session is told what is remembered, taught how to add to it, or answered when it asks. Everything kept stays here, listed and searchable.

add.title: Remember something
add.secretRefused: That looks like it carries a key, token or password, so it was not saved. Memory goes into every later prompt and into your project folders.
add.noProjectRefused: This memory is scoped to a project, and no project was chosen, so it was not saved. Pick a project or keep it everywhere.
add.blankRefused: There is nothing to remember here yet.

groups.unknownProject: A project that no longer exists
groups.forgetProjectConfirmDescription: The project these memories belong to no longer exists, so no session is ever shown them. This cannot be undone.

row.forgetConfirmDescription: "{{text}}" will no longer be carried into future sessions. This cannot be undone.
row.crowdedOut: crowded out — still found by search and recall
row.openAgentChat: Open the chat that wrote this
row.sessionGone: The chat that wrote this is no longer here.

access.title: Who can write here
access.operator: You, in any ordinary chat — always.
access.conductor: A conductor — always. Its whole job is to hold what a request taught it.
access.orchestrator: An orchestrator — only when its agent carries the memory-write permission.
access.worker: A worker, and every executor a wave spawns — never. Its report goes through the conductor, and that loop is where anything it learned belongs.
